inventory.visualPurpose: Respiratory burst — the phagolysosome enzyme cascade diagram
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: A vector pathway diagram inside a Phagolysosome containing Bacteria: six numbered steps — (1) NADPH oxidase on the Neutrophil cell membrane (O2 + NADPH → O2⁻; NADPH oxidase deficiency = chronic granulomatous disease), (2) Superoxide dismutase (O2⁻ → H2O2), (3) Myeloperoxidase (H2O2 + Cl⁻ → HOCl, hypochlorite bleach), (4) Catalase/glutathione peroxidase (H2O2 → H2O + O2, also via bacterial catalase), (5) Glutathione reductase (GSH/GSSG cycling), (6) G6PD (Glucose-6-P → 6-phosphogluconolactone, NADPH from HMP shunt) — with legends for superoxide, HOCl, and glutathione states.

notes: Census: pure vector page (zero rasters). The phagolysosome cascade diagram is redrawn as ONE original KYP registry visual (respiratory-burst-enzymes) with all six numbered steps and their legends accounted for (15 label quotes verified), plus the CGD-logic and type I IFN panels. Verbatim text is the note's table block.
